• Described by Achille Valenciennes in 1840.
  • Common name: Veined catfish
  • Synonym: Tachysurus venosus
  • IUCN Red List: Not Evaluated
Indo-West Pacific: Mozambique Channel to Burma (Myanmar) and southern China to Indonesia (excluding the Philippines and Australia). Found in the Mekong delta.

It inhabits tropical marine and brackish waters in the Indo-western Pacific region, including the Mozambique Channel, Myanmar, Indonesia and southern China. Marine; brackish; demersal; depth range 20–50 m. Tropical. It dwells at a depth range of 20 to 50 m.
Feeds mainly on invertebrates and small fishes.

It reaches a maximum total length of 30 cm, but more commonly about 19 cm TL. Etymology: the specific name venosus means veiny, referring to the vein-like latero-sensory canals. Remarks: captured mainly with bamboo traps and set bagnets.
